title: IAU 2015 B3: nominal solar constants are exact conversion values, not best estimates
summary: Resolution B3 defines nominal solar radius, irradiance, luminosity, effective temperature, and GM as exact SI values, and says they are not current best estimates.
body: The text of IAU 2015 Resolution B3, as printed in Mamajek and colleagues, adopts nominal conversion constants that are defined to be exact SI values. The resolution says the nominal constants are based on current best estimates, which have uncertainties, are not secularly constant, and are updated, and that the nominal constants should be interpreted as standard values and not as those best estimates. The adopted solar values printed in the resolution table are: nominal solar radius 6.957 × 10^8 m; nominal total solar irradiance 1361 W m^-2; nominal solar luminosity 3.828 × 10^26 W; nominal solar effective temperature 5772 K; nominal solar mass parameter (GM) 1.327 124 4 × 10^20 m^3 s^-2. A mass in nominal solar masses is the ratio of GM values. If an SI mass is needed, the resolution says to divide by a stated value of G, and it gives the 2014 CODATA example G = 6.67408 (±0.00031) × 10^−11 m^3 kg^-1 s^-2. These nominal numbers are definitions for conversion. They are not a new measurement.
